newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-EBADIYLA GIVES MURTAGH FIRST CLASSIC WIN.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-EBADIYLA GIVES MURTAGH FIRST CLASSIC WIN.

text.p: Ebadiyla, sixth in the Epsom
Oaks, gained rich compensation on Sunday with victory in the
Irish equivalent at The Curragh.
The Aga Khan's filly, a 9-2 chance ridden by John Murtagh,
took up the running inside the final furlong to beat the 6-4
favourite Yashmak, the mount of Kieren Fallon, by three lengths.
French trained Brilliance, 5-1 and ridden by Sylvain
Guillot, was a further head away third in the 11-runner field.
Ebadiyla's stablemate Aliya cut out much of the early
running in the 1-1/2 miles (2.4 km) race with Caiseal Ros in
close attention and Yashmak held up the middle of the field.
Turning for home, Fallon produced Yashmak on the outside to
take up the running, but Murtagh made a well-timed move on the
rails which put Ebadiyla ahead and gave him his first classic
success.
It ended a week of mixed fortunes for Fallon, who was
heavily criticised for his riding of Bosra Sham in the Eclipse
Stakes at Sandown eight days ago. But he has been in sparkling
form since and ridden 14 winners.
Fallon did nothing wrong on this occasion but was beaten by
a better filly on the day.
Trainer Aiden O'Brien, hoping for a fourth successive Irish
classic triumph after winning the Irish 1,000 and 2,000 Guineas
and the Irish Derby earlier this year, had to be content with
fourth place from 6-1 chance Strawberry Roan, one of his three
entries.
